title: Question 1
statement_text: Is it true that for every graph class $\mathcal{C}$ with polynomial expansion, there exists a polynomial function $f$ such that for every integer $r\geqslant 0$ and every graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$, $$\mathrm{scol}_{r}(G)\leqslant f(r)?$$
context_text: Esperet and Raymond asked whether polynomial expansion of a graph class implies polynomial strong $r$-coloring numbers. A positive answer would yield a new characterization of polynomial expansion in terms of polynomial strong coloring numbers. The present paper introduces four new bounded-radius parameters (depth-$r$ bramble number, tangle number, linkedness, well-linkedness) hoping they provide tools toward a positive answer.
paper_contribution: Introduces depth-$r$ bramble number, tangle number, linkedness, and well-linkedness, proves they are pairwise polynomially related and all polynomially bounded in $r$ for classes with polynomial expansion, providing potential new tools toward resolving the question positively.

title: Question 2
statement_text: Is it true that for every graph class $\mathcal{C}$ with polynomial expansion, there exists a polynomial function $f$ such that for every integer $r\geqslant 0$ and every graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$, $$\mathrm{scol}_{r}(G)\leqslant f(r,\mathrm{bn}_{r}(G))?$$
context_text: A graph $H$ is a depth-$r$ minor of $G$ if it is obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs of radius at most $r$; $\nabla_r(G)$ is the maximum of $|E(H)|/|V(H)|$ over depth-$r$ minors $H$ of $G$, and a class $\mathcal{C}$ has polynomial expansion if $\nabla_r(G)\le f(r)$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, $r\ge0$, for some polynomial $f$. Given a linear order $\pi$ of $V(G)$, a vertex $u$ is strongly $r$-reachable from $v$ if $\pi(u)\le\pi(v)$ and some path of length at most $r$ joins $v$ to $u$ with all internal vertices $w$ satisfying $\pi(w)>\pi(v)$; the strong $r$-coloring number $\mathrm{scol}_r(G)$ is the minimum over $\pi$ of the maximum over $v$ of the number of vertices strongly $r$-reachable from $v$. Two vertex sets touch if they share a vertex or are joined by an edge; a bramble is a set of pairwise touching connected vertex sets, its order is the minimum size of a set meeting all its elements, and a depth-$r$ bramble is one whose elements each induce a subgraph of radius at most $r$; the depth-$r$ bramble number $\mathrm{bn}_r(G)$ is the maximum order of a depth-$r$ bramble ($\mathrm{bn}_\infty(G)=\mathrm{scol}_\infty(G)$ is treewidth plus one). The authors prove $\mathrm{bn}_r(G)\le\mathrm{scol}_{4r+1}(G)$, and that in a class with polynomial expansion $\mathrm{bn}_r$ (and the related depth-$r$ tangle number, linkedness and well-linkedness) is bounded by a polynomial in $r$. A positive answer to this question would therefore answer positively the open problem of Joret and Wood asking whether every class with polynomial expansion has strong $r$-coloring numbers bounded by a polynomial in $r$ (which would characterize polynomial expansion). The polynomial expansion assumption is essential: over all graphs, $\mathrm{scol}_r(G)$ cannot be bounded by any function of $r$ and $\mathrm{bn}_{g(r)}(G)$, for any function $g$ (graphs of large minimum degree and large girth have $\mathrm{bn}_s(G)=2$).

title: Question 13
statement_text: Is it true that for every graph class $\mathcal{C}$ with polynomial expansion, there exists a polynomial function $f$ such that for every integer $r\geqslant 0$ and every graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$, $$\mathrm{scol}_{r}(G)\leqslant f(r,\mathrm{grid}_{\mathrm{poly}(r)}(G))?$$
context_text: For $r=\infty$, grid minors are intimately related to $\mathrm{scol}_r$ via treewidth, but for finite $r$ this connection breaks down: for every $r,k\geqslant 1$ and every non-forest $H$, there exist graphs without $H$ as a depth-$k$ minor but with arbitrarily large strong $r$-coloring number. The question asks whether the connection survives when restricted to classes with polynomial expansion.
